messages:
sally (support): FYI incoming customer escalation — intermittent SSE disconnects + truncated streams when client refreshes auth. They see 1-2 partial messages then the stream drops. Customer: AcmePay.

sally (support): Error snippets from their side: `ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_ERROR code=ECONNRESET` and our proxy shows `upstream closed connection` around same time. They say it correlates with token refresh at ~55s. :thinking:

matt (eng-oncall): Thanks. Any tracing ids or request ids? can you grab a few root request ids and approximate wallclock times?

sally (support): Provided 3 request ids in the ticket: r123, r124, r125. Local timestamps attached. They mentioned client-side keepalive set to 60s.

alice (frontend): Quick theory: client CRL refresh (rotate token) may close the SSE connection then re-open; during the gap they get truncated output. If the client doesn't reattach last-event-id we could lose ephemeral partial output and trigger duplicate billing for resumed tokens.

bob (infra): Also possible: ALB idle timeout = 60s default -> if client keepalive intervals are > ALB idle, ALB may drop TCP before client sees it. That would look like upstream closed. What are our proxy timeouts?

matt (eng-oncall): Proxy config: nginx sidecar idle_timeout=75s, gateway idle=120s, but external LB (cloud) idle is 60s. So mismatch exists.

sally (support): Customer reported gap when rotating token at ~55s, which fits a 60s LB idle.

paul (billing): Heads-up — if the client reconnects within same session but without dedupe, they get billed for both partial and resumed outputs. We saw one customer double-billed. Need to confirm billing logic around resumed SSE fragments.

alice (frontend): Repro steps I ran locally: 1) open stream, 2) send long completion 200 tokens, 3) block network for 3s at 56s, 4) resume. Outcome: client sees partial then reconnect creates new stream, server generates overlapping tokens.

alice (frontend): Attached small repro script using fetch + AbortController that flips network. snippet:
```js
const s = await fetch('/v1/stream', {headers:{Authorization: 'Bearer X'}});
// wait 56s
// abort + re-open with last-event-id
```

bob (infra): Good repro. Two mitigations: 1) push opinionated shorter comment-ping (SSE comment) interval from client (eg 15s) so LB sees activity, or 2) change LB idle to 180s for streaming routes. Both have tradeoffs.

matt (eng-oncall): Also consider server-side soft-close: send periodic `: keepalive\n\n` comments at 10-20s from the server runtime so the TCP layer is active independent of client behavior. But must test with proxies that strip comments.

sally (support): Customer asked for immediate workaround — suggested they lower their token refresh window to happen off-stream and enable client-side SSE comment pings at 20s. They asked if we can do server-side change without infra rollout.

bob (infra): We can enable server comment pings in runtime config flag for hosted customers without infra changes. Will need to run a small rollout to 5% first. Impact on billing negligible.

paul (billing): If we enable server pings, log line must include original request id so post-processor can dedupe resumed streams. Otherwise accounting will double count.

matt (eng-oncall): Action items: 1) bob to enable runtime server comment pings behind flag and add request-id header in ping logs (ETA 48h). 2) alice to validate client repro with comment pings and last-event-id behavior. 3) sally to communicate workaround to customer (reduce refresh, client ping). 4) paul to add dedupe rule for resumed sessions if same upstream request id within 10s.

bob (infra): I'll spin the feature branch: `sse/periodic-comment-pings` and add config: `sse.ping_interval_ms=20000` by default for streaming routes. Will add log: `sse_ping request_id=<id> upstream_ts=<ts>`.

repro-bot: automated note: ran scheduled repro job against AcmePay with 20s server pings, saw 0 disconnects in 30 runs.

alice (frontend): I ran the local script against dev with server pings enabled — reconnect no longer truncates; last-event-id resume works and we don't see overlapping outputs.

sally (support): Customer accepted workaround; they will delay token rotation off-stream and test server pings. I'll keep ticket open until next week. Thanks team :pray:

matt (eng-oncall): Follow-up: we should add a short runbook entry summarizing LB client keepalive mismatch and server ping mitigation in docs/support/runbooks/streaming-keepalive.md (small TODO).

paul (billing): I'll schedule a quick job to scan recent streaming sessions for duplicated billing events and reconcile any affected customers.

bob (infra): Rolling out flag to 5% now — will update when platform shows green.

sally (support): Closing loop: customer confirmed stable after pings. Leaving ticket monitored for 24h then will mark resolved. :white_check_mark:
